claims.statement: The European Commission states that the CBAM definitive regime applies from 1 January 2026 and covers cement, iron and steel, aluminium, fertilisers, electricity, and hydrogen.

The Commission states that EU importers above a single 50-tonne mass threshold must apply for authorised CBAM declarant status, buy certificates, declare embedded emissions, and may deduct a proven carbon price paid abroad.

Inference: the combination of threshold status, supplier evidence, and a variable certificate price creates a recurring finance-data problem for importers that is separable from customs filing itself.

contrary_evidence: Importers at or below the 50-tonne threshold are outside the authorisation requirement, sharply narrowing the small-business pool.
Large importers, customs brokers, and ERP vendors may already have reporting and forecasting capability.
Default values can reduce the immediate need to collect granular supplier data, depending on the applicable rules and cost tradeoff.

economics.acquisition_route: Revenue share with customs brokers plus content-led calculators targeted to specific commodity and volume bands
economics.founder_net_worth_path: Scenario, not evidence: 1,000 EU importers at PLN 30,000 annual recurring revenue yields PLN 30m revenue; a 35% operating margin and several years of distributions could create PLN 20m-30m founder net worth without external capital or an exit
economics.founder_time: Four hours per day during a five-customer pilot, capped by accepting only one commodity family until exception rates are measurable
economics.gross_margin_basis: Automated customs-line mapping and recurring forecasts can approach 75% gross margin; supplier chasing and expert review are the main variable costs
economics.payback: Target immediate to three months because the paid historical-data cleanup should fund onboarding labour and broker commission
economics.pricing: Assumption: PLN 7,500-20,000 onboarding and PLN 1,500-4,000 per month, with a separately priced annual declaration review
economics.retention_or_repeat: Every covered shipment refreshes exposure and every compliance year creates a declaration cycle; retention depends on remaining more useful than a broker spreadsheet

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: A growing cross-supplier graph of CN codes, production routes, usable emissions fields, default-value fallbacks, and recurring correction patterns that shortens each new importer setup
fingerprint.customer: Polish and neighbouring-EU importers of roughly 50 to 2,000 tonnes per year of iron, steel, aluminium, cement, fertilisers, or hydrogen, with a lean finance and customs function
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: White-label referrals from customs brokers, freight forwarders, and metal or fertiliser trade advisers, supported by a self-serve landed-cost calculator
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: Managed data service plus SaaS that maps customs lines to covered goods, requests and quality-scores supplier emissions files, estimates certificate exposure, and preserves an audit trail; entity subscription with volume tiers
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: The importer's finance or customs lead pays at onboarding when the first twelve months of customs lines are reconciled, then pays monthly for shipment forecasts and annually for a declaration evidence pack
fingerprint.problem_trigger: The CBAM definitive regime applies from 1 January 2026 and importers above the single 50-tonne mass threshold must become authorised declarants, declare embedded emissions, and surrender certificates

founder_fit: Carbon-cost forecasting and messy supplier-data reconciliation use analytical and finance strengths
A customs-broker channel can replace meeting-heavy direct enterprise sales
The product can start with file uploads and one commodity before any expensive integration
Poland is a practical beachhead while the same EU regime supports multilingual expansion
risks: Incorrect goods or emissions mapping could cause certificate under-purchase or reporting errors.
Human supplier follow-up could overwhelm a five-hour daily schedule.
Regulatory simplification may further shrink covered volume or data granularity.
Sensitive procurement and cost data require strong isolation, access control, and audit logging.

structure.commercial_archetype: Managed regulatory data pipeline with recurring landed-cost analytics
structure.control_point: The pre-order and pre-customs decision where embedded-carbon evidence changes supplier choice and cash needs
structure.critical_dependency: Reliable supplier emissions evidence, current default values and certificate prices, and correct goods-scope mapping

thesis: A managed data pipeline for EU importers just above the 50-tonne CBAM threshold can reconcile customs lines, supplier emissions evidence, default values, certificate-price exposure, and annual declaration support. The buyer is not the largest industrial group with an internal carbon team but a finance or import manager whose first irreversible decision is whether a shipment remains profitable after embedded-carbon cost.
title: CBAM Landed-Cost and Supplier-Data Desk for Mid-Market Importers
uncertainties: A bottom-up count of target importers by commodity, annual tonnage, and current solution has not been established.
No willingness-to-pay evidence supports the proposed pricing or the 1,000-customer wealth scenario.
The labour required to obtain acceptable foreign-supplier data is unknown.
The boundary between software output and regulated customs or verification advice needs legal review.
